stopLine: Do not treat missing password configuration as authorization, create a second device for the remote shortcut, guess a phone model, merge credentials by model, overwrite a user rename, expose a public internet route, or substitute automated tests for target-phone acceptance.
evidenceRefs: README defines QR-only authorization, one phone-to-computer identity, durable trusted-device behavior, repeated-scan identity reuse, local and remote shortcut origins mapped to one device, password-free reopen, revocation, and truthful model-first names.

Structured decision LAN-TRUSTED-DEVICE-001 records QR as the only authorization route, no password bypass, persistent credentials, the same identity for local and remote shortcut origins, and model-first names without guessing or merging.

An unpaired request is rejected even without legacy password configuration, password POST is disabled, QR tickets are one-time, and the existing identity mechanism can adopt a trusted device across stable or Tailscale origins instead of creating a duplicate.

The current branch candidate contains QR-only authorization, persistent rolling credentials, device management, repeated-scan reuse, cross-origin adoption without a new row, model-first naming, and tests. The two-shortcut UI is tracked by PHONE-ONE-SCAN-001 and DESKTOP-TRAY-WEB-CONSOLE-001.
Server and client typechecks passed on 2026-08-28 with QR-only authorization and preferred-origin migration enabled.

Sixteen test files and fifty-two tests passed, including rejection of unpaired requests without a password, one-primary-QR API shape, concurrent one-time origin migration tickets, persistent trusted-device identity, repeated-scan reuse, cross-origin adoption without a new row, Tailscale address classification, model naming, and revocation.
A temporary device authenticated before and after a production service restart, failed immediately after revocation, and was removed without changing the nine existing trusted devices on 2026-08-27.

The trusted-device count moved from 10 to 11 on first pairing, stayed 11 after rescanning the same QR, stayed 11 after a fresh-origin session adopted the stable-link identity, authenticated successfully, and returned to 10 after removing the temporary device on 2026-08-27.

The deployed portable package returned SM-S9280 from an Android Build User-Agent, 23127PN0CC from Sec-CH-UA-Model when the reduced User-Agent exposed only K, and the truthful fallback iPhone when no exact Apple model was available. Live trusted-device count stayed 2 and its file hash was unchanged.

The deployed candidate at release/deployed-qr-tailscale-20260828-193855 reports pairingOnly=true and authenticated=false without a cookie, rejects an old-password POST with HTTP 403, renders only the scan instruction with no password field, and preserves the two-device file at SHA-256 85436A7D983FF6B126E314FB6279C2AB3278EF9921C3495D3F7323DB0BF6C1F1.
